🟡 Current Updates: November 23-24, 2026 🇾🇪 Yemen Saudi airstrikes across Yemen continued, causing civilian casualties and targeting multiple areas. The Sanaa Health Ministry reported that 12 civilians were killed and 47 wounded in 48 hours of Saudi aggression, including three children among the dead and three children and seven women among the wounded. Since the beginning of the escalation, the ministry’s reported toll has risen to 450 killed and 971 wounded. Saudi warplanes carried out three airstrikes on Jabal al-Salal, east of Taiz, followed by six airstrikes targeting the Al-Misrakh and Hayfan districts of Taiz, including the isolated Al-Aboos area, which was reportedly struck for the fifth time. Saudi aircraft also bombed the Al-Maqatirah district in Lahij Governorate, where local sources reported 25 killed or missing and six wounded in an initial toll following strikes on the Mabaq Valley area. Further airstrikes targeted the port city of Hodeidah and Sanaa. Meanwhile, the Yemeni Armed Forces launched drone attacks against targets in southern Saudi Arabia, with Saudi authorities acknowledging the attacks. Alerts and sirens were reported in Abha and Jazan, while further Yemeni attacks reportedly targeted Najran and Al-Sulayil in Saudi Arabia. 🇮🇷 Iran Approximately 30 cases of methanol poisoning were reported in Shiraz and Marvdasht within 24 hours, resulting in one death. The Deputy of Treatment at Shiraz University of Medical Sciences issued a serious warning after patients presented symptoms of poisoning from industrial alcohol. The Tehran Province Intelligence Organization of the IRGC discovered and dismantled an illegal cryptocurrency mining facility in Islamshahr. The operation involved 143 mining devices powered by natural gas, with a reported electricity consumption capacity of 458 kilowatts. Investigations indicated that the facility had generated more than four million kilowatt-hours of energy using natural gas, equivalent to the monthly electricity consumption of more than 13,000 households during the summer. 🇵🇸 Palestine Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip continued, killing and wounding Palestinians. Three Palestinians were killed in shelling and gunfire across various areas on Sunday. Israeli forces demolished residential buildings east of Gaza City overnight, while intense gunfire from Israeli military vehicles was reported east of Khan Yunis, particularly in the Batn al-Samin area, and east of Al-Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza. A Palestinian was also wounded in the foot by Israeli gunfire near the Asda intersection, west of Khan Yunis. Three Palestinians were killed in an Israeli strike targeting a vehicle west of Gaza City. The victims were identified as Khalil Sobhi Kahil, 35, Raed Jamal Al-Masry, 38, and Ahmed Al-Zaharna, 28. Russia is also believed to be a possible culprit of the attacks, which have included warnings and bomb threats against some vessels. Targeted ships were operating close to Europe and Asia at the time of the attacks, and at least four ships were assisted by the U.S. Coast Guard on their approach to the U.S. The risk is that a nefarious actor could compromise integrated systems which the vessels depend on, and through them cause am explosion, collision or oil spill. The attacks could have the aim of disrupting critical maritime routes or cause an explosion at a major port far from the Middle East.
